newsitem.title: CHILE: NOVA in third Chile natgas pipeline talks.
newsitem.headline: NOVA in third Chile natgas pipeline talks.

text.p: Canadian gas firm NOVA Corp said it hopes to sign up customers by year-end for a natural gas pipeline the firm is planning to build from Argentina across the Andes to southern Chile.
"We are in talks and hope to sign sales contracts by the end of the year," Gabriel Leon, senior vice-president of NovaGas International Ltda told Reuters.

If it goes ahead, the project will be NOVA's third pipeline linking the two countries and is in addition to the GasAndes scheme in central Chile and the Gas de Atacama project which crosses the northern Atacama Desert.
The GasAndes pipeline, part-owned by Chilean generator Chilgener, is under contruction and NOVA is carrying out a feasibility study on the Gas de Atacama scheme.
The Gas de Sur pipeline will run from the gasfields of Neuquen in southern Argentina to the industrial city of Concepcion in Chile's Eighth Region.

Construction of the pipeline, which will cost around $350 million, is due to begin next year with project coming on stream in 1998, said Leon who was in Santiago to attend a regional energy conference.
The pipeline will supply energy to industrial customers in Concepcion and to a gas-fired electricity generator which will be built in the region, he said.
